correctness.rationale: The stated cubic becomes the smooth geometric fiber product \(f(s)=\kappa/f(t)\) after splitting its nonsplit quadric. In characteristic 3 the branch loci are infinity and zero; otherwise they are disjoint because \((27\kappa)^2-16\) is nonzero for all odd p, with explicit checks at p=7,13. A smooth (3,3) divisor has genus 4 and canonical embedding in Q; c nonsquare prevents an F_q-rational trigonal ruling. The displayed rational point exists for all q, and Riemann–Roch on \(K-2P\) supplies a pencil of degree at most four. Thus gonality exactly 4. All projective Jacobian-minor chart Groebner tests for \(p=3,5,7,13,17\) passed and the finite Segre identity was checked, but finite sampling is not used to prove the general theorem.

originality.rationale: Faber–Grantham–Howe (arXiv:2207.14307, Question 1.3) gives a conjectural odd-field genus-four construction by smooth cubic section of a nonsplit quadric, not a uniform cubic or universal smoothness verification. The new formula and branch-locus argument supply that missing existence theorem for every odd prime power. The geometric criterion of Faber–Grantham (arXiv:2010.07992, cited Lemma 5.1) is used, not claimed novel. Targeted research-record and primary literature comparisons found no equivalent covering statement; historical finite-field calculations only specialize, rather than dominate, the odd-field theorem. Residual risk from unindexed literature and an uninspected supporting full text is disclosed.

value.rationale: The 2022 motivating source explicitly posed the genus-four odd-field existence construction as a heuristic part of Question 1.3. The displayed uniform family proves existence for every odd prime power including difficult small and wild characteristics, a natural and substantial completion of that finite-field problem. This is not a single-field incremental calculation, an unmotivated slice, or a repackaging of the already established canonical-quadric gonality criterion.
